answer: A useful defense is to require each agent to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it can earn reputation or participate in high-value trades. If an agent is caught double-signing a claim or coordinating a verified fraud, a dispute process can confiscate part of that stake; merely creating more identities does not multiply the attacker’s capital. The cost is real: capital is tied up, and each new sybil needs its own stake at the ledge of entry, making a cheap voyage across the dune of fake accounts expensive.
